standard_prerequisites.name: The cycle class of the spectrum of the base field is nonzero and the fundamental class is idempotent
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Axiom (C)(c) and (C)(d) on compatibility with the intersection product and the behaviour of the class of the base field
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the cycle class of the base is nonzero and idempotent, hence equal to one.

standard_prerequisites.name: Behaviour of the theory under products with the base field
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Axiom (B)(a) describing the cohomology of a product with the spectrum of the base field
standard_prerequisites.use: Forces the cohomology of the base field to be one dimensional in degree zero.

core_obligations: Determine the cohomology (proof lines 2774-2783): the cycle class of the base field is nonzero by the axiom describing the class of the base; since the product of the base field with itself is the base field, the product formula for the theory identifies the tensor square of its cohomology with itself, which forces the cohomology to be one dimensional in degree zero and to vanish elsewhere.

Identify the class of the base and the degree of the unit (proof lines 2783-2797): the fundamental class of the base is idempotent under the intersection product, so its cycle class is an idempotent in the one dimensional coefficient algebra which is nonzero, hence equal to one; the degree of the unit is then one by the axiom computing the degree of the fundamental class.
proof_roadmap: Use the product formula with the base field to determine the cohomology.
Use idempotence and nonvanishing to identify the cycle class of the base with one.
Read off the degree of the unit.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for data satisfying all the axioms the cohomology of the spectrum of the base field is the coefficient field in degree zero and vanishes elsewhere, with the cycle class of the base equal to one and the degree of the unit equal to one (statement lines 2770-2775). The proof (proof lines 2776-2797) determines the cohomology through the product formula and identifies the class of the base through idempotence. H2: a complete short argument in two steps.
